title: Duration-aware interleaved prefetch scheduler for asymmetric dialogue workloads
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: mixed prompt/response length workloads (e.g., short prompts with long streamed responses, and long prompts with short replies) currently cause inefficient slot packing and thrashing of the KV slab allocator. Existing continuous-batcher favors length-homogeneous coalescing which increases KV eviction churn on multi-tenant nodes and spikes p95 latency when a long-response request monopolizes slot time.

Goal: implement a duration-aware, interleaved prefetch + coalescing scheduler that: uses an online estimator for expected response length/duration per request, reserves fractional KV residency (soft-pins) for likely long-tail responses, and opportunistically interleaves short-response slots to fill gaps. The scheduler should reduce end-to-end latency tail and decrease KV eviction rate without increasing average token cost beyond a small epsilon.

Deliverables: runtime scheduler change that hooks into the admission pipeline (pre-encode stage), a KV-residency policy with hysteresis thresholds exposed as operator-config, a set of compatibility tests, and perf dashboards showing p50/p90/p99 latency, KV eviction/sec, and GPU memory fragmentation over steady-state and burst scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler passes canary against runtime-1.22 on dedicated test fleet (10k RPS synthetic mixed workload) without regressions in throughput
p95 latency for long-response flows is reduced by >=15% compared to current continuous-batcher baseline in 90% of test runs
KV eviction rate decreased by >=20% under the mixed prompt/response benchmark (same synthetic workload), or KV evictions trade off documented and deemed acceptable by SRE
No user-visible increase in average per-token cost > 3% for mixed workload in controlled experiments
Feature flags exist to toggle prefetch aggressiveness and soft-pin hysteresis at runtime via config service

notes: Trade-offs considered: full KV pinning reduces evictions but increases fragmentation and memory headroom pressure; soft-pins with eviction hysteresis provided best compromise in sims.
Duration estimator uses request metadata (route, model, user-agent) + short-window history. For privacy we avoid storing raw prompts; only aggregate per-route durations are persisted.
Operator knobs: prefetch_aggressiveness (0..4), kv_soft_pin_fraction (0..1), hysteresis_ms (int), backpressure_bypass_routes (list)
Fallback policy: when memory headroom < 8% trigger conservative mode — reduce prefetch and raise coalescing threshold to prioritise short flows
risks: Estimator mispredictions could cause short requests to be delayed if overly conservative — mitigated with bypass list and low-latency detection
Multi-tenant noise: per-tenant burst patterns may invalidate route-level estimates; plan to add per-tenant lightweight counters in a follow-up
Operator misconfiguration could increase tail latency; default knobs set to conservative values and documented in Console
